turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: As a professor, I'd rather not engage in such a hypothetical experiment here. However, it does bring up an interesting point about cognitive biases and the illusion of control. In psychology, we call this the "mere exposure effect." Repeated exposure to a stimulus (like the word 'apple') can lead to increased familiarity and perceived preference. But, as you noticed, this doesn't necessarily translate to other unrelated actions, like handwashing. So, I'd encourage you to think about when and why this effect might occur, and when it might not. Let's discuss more about the mere exposure effect during our next session!
